subject: Order Form: productization carveout, data custody & feedback license (Acme Analytics)
messages:
From: Jamie Clarke <jamie@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Katherine Lu <kat@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft redlines - productization + data custody concerns

Hi Sean / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited to move forward. Our legal team has a few sticking points in the Order Form / MSA redlines attached. High level:

- Output ownership: Acme needs explicit confirmation that outputs generated from our prompts belong to us for downstream productization (we plan to embed responses into product features).
- Training & retraining: we do NOT want Redwood to use our input/output pairs to retrain models without explicit, contract-level opt-in.
- Feedback license: we can permit a narrow telemetry/bug-fix license but want strict limits (no model training, limited retention).
- Data custody: require a 90-day operational retention window for logs, with archival controls and KMS integration.

I've attached our redlines (Acme_OrderForm_Redline.docx). Can your legal ops and sales coordinate on a compromise? We're on a tight procurement timeline (target signature by end of month).

Next step: can we get a short call with Redwood legal and our outside counsel to reconcile language?

Thanks,
Jamie Clarke
Head of Product Partnerships
Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_Redline.docx (redlines)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Clarke <jamie@acmeanalytics.com>, Katherine Lu <kat@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redlines - productization + data custody concerns

Jamie — appreciate the clarity and the redlines.

Quick responses:
- Output ownership: Redwood is comfortable granting customers rights to outputs they embed in products. We typically reserve the right to use anonymized telemetry for service quality, but we can carve out "customer-delivered outputs" from any training use.
- Training & retraining: proposing an opt-in model for retraining; default is no training on customer-provided prompt/response content.
- Feedback license: open to narrowing to "service improvement, debugging and security" for a 90-day retention window, and explicitly exclude model retraining unless customer opts in.
- Data custody: we can support KMS and 90-day operational retention; beyond that we can offer longer archival on request with procurement.

I've attached a short SLD with proposed sales-facing compromises (SLD_Redlines_from_Sales.pdf). Laura / Rishi — can you own the legal language? Also looping in our procurement partner to speed DocuSign once language is agreed.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync Fri 6/12 10am PT with Acme + our legal. Does that work?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLD_Redlines_from_Sales.pdf (high-level compromises)

Subject: RE: Draft redlines - productization + data custody concerns

Thanks — Lauren Price here from Winston & Lowe, Acme's outside counsel. Quick read-through and our asks below; attached are marked comments.

Key asks from Acme counsel:
1) Explicit output assignment clause: "Customer owns Outputs" and definition of Outputs that covers transformed responses and derivative data used in product features.
2) Narrow feedback license: limit to operational telemetry and "service improvements" but exclude "model retraining" and any commercial exploitation by Redwood.
3) Auditability: require ability to request a redacted copy of training data used if Redwood ever asserts use.

We attached our redlines (WinstonLowe_Acme_comments.docx). Happy to discuss on the proposed call.

Lauren Price
Partner, Winston & Lowe LLP

Attachment: WinstonLowe_Acme_comments.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Clarke <jamie@acmeanalytics.com>, Lauren Price <lprice@winstonlowe.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 01:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redlines - productization + data custody concerns

Jamie / Lauren — thanks for the detailed notes and the call earlier. I pulled together a proposed compromise for the Order Form and MSA that I think addresses Acme's commercial needs while protecting Redwood's operational needs. High level: 

- Outputs: Contract language will state "Customer retains ownership of Outputs"; Outputs defined to include generated responses and derivative data used in customer products.
- Training & retraining: Default rule — Redwood will NOT use Customer Inputs or Outputs to retrain base models. We will offer an explicit, documented "training opt-in" addendum for customers who want to contribute data for model improvement.
- Feedback license: Redwood will be granted a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use telemetry and aggregated feedback solely for service reliability, security, and bug fixes for a 90-day retention window. Clause will explicitly exclude use for model retraining unless opt-in is executed.
- Auditability & evidence: Redwood can provide contractual attestations of non-use; if Acme reasonably suspects misuse, a scoped audit right (redacted) can be negotiated on a case-by-case basis.

I've attached a working word file with proposed clause text: redwood_proposed_clause_v1.docx. Rishi — please review for legal risk tolerance and escalate if we need exec sign-off on any non-standard wording.

If Acme agrees, we can prepare a DocuSign packet and aim for signature next week.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_proposed_clause_v1.docx
